en.text:
Today’s M&A briefing — 3 deals, the strategies behind them · 27 October 2026

🔹 EQT (natural gas exploration and production in the Appalachia, North America) merges with Range Resources (independent natural gas exploration and production in the Appalachia, long-life reserve portfolio) — $50bn.
Our view: EQT positions itself as a key player for the next phase of natural gas demand — data centers, LNG exports, industrial energy transition — by integrating the end-to-end chain to capture margin at each step.

🔹 Intel Corporation (chip design and manufacturing, development of silicon spin qubits produced with conventional manufacturing processes) acquires Classiq (software platform for automatic synthesis of quantum algorithms, qubit technology-agnostic, based in Tel Aviv).
Intel has been developing silicon spin qubits since 2015 using its conventional manufacturing equipment. Classiq provides the software abstraction layer that allows developers to write quantum programs without manually manipulating circuits at the qubit level.
Our view: The acquisition of Classiq shifts the focus of quantum computing: the question is no longer which hardware technology will win, but who controls the software layer that makes it usable by an ordinary developer.

🔹 Procede Software (publisher of Excede® DMS for truck, trailer, bus, and aftermarket dealerships) acquires RIMSS (publisher of DMS for agricultural, construction, and transport dealerships, OEM integrations with Kubota, Case IH, AGCO, and Hino).
Both platforms are built on Microsoft technology. Many dealership groups operate both truck (Excede) and agricultural or construction (RIMSS) businesses. Both companies boast a customer retention rate of approximately 99%.
Our view: The complementarity is direct: bringing both DMS under one publisher simplifies contracts, integrations, and support for multi-activity groups that already used both platforms separately.

🔹 EQT (𝑒𝑥𝑝𝑙𝑜𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑑𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑔𝑎𝑧 𝑛𝑎𝑡𝑢𝑟𝑒𝑙 𝑑𝑎𝑛𝑠 𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝐴𝑝𝑝𝑎𝑙𝑎𝑐ℎ𝑒𝑠, 𝐴𝑚𝑒́𝑟𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑑𝑢 𝑁𝑜𝑟𝑑) fusionne avec Range Resources (𝑒𝑥𝑝𝑙𝑜𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑝𝑟𝑜𝑑𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑔𝑎𝑧𝑖𝑒̀𝑟𝑒 𝑖𝑛𝑑𝑒́𝑝𝑒𝑛𝑑𝑎𝑛𝑡𝑒 𝑑𝑎𝑛𝑠 𝑙𝑒𝑠 𝐴𝑝𝑝𝑎𝑙𝑎𝑐ℎ𝑒𝑠, 𝑝𝑜𝑟𝑡𝑒𝑓𝑒𝑢𝑖𝑙𝑙𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑟𝑒́𝑠𝑒𝑟𝑣𝑒𝑠 𝑎̀ 𝑙𝑜𝑛𝑔𝑢𝑒 𝑑𝑢𝑟𝑒́𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑣𝑖𝑒) — 50 Md$.
Point de vue : EQT se positionne comme interlocuteur incontournable pour la prochaine phase de demande en gaz naturel — data centers, exportations de GNL, transition énergétique industrielle — en intégrant la chaîne de bout en bout pour capter la marge à chaque étape.

🔹 Intel Corporation (𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑐𝑒𝑝𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑓𝑎𝑏𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑑𝑒 𝑝𝑢𝑐𝑒𝑠) rachète Classiq (𝑝𝑙𝑎𝑡𝑒𝑓𝑜𝑟𝑚𝑒 𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑐𝑖𝑒𝑙𝑙𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑠𝑦𝑛𝑡ℎ𝑒̀𝑠𝑒 𝑎𝑢𝑡𝑜𝑚𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑑'𝑎𝑙𝑔𝑜𝑟𝑖𝑡ℎ𝑚𝑒𝑠 𝑞𝑢𝑎𝑛𝑡𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠, 𝑎𝑔𝑛𝑜𝑠𝑡𝑖𝑞𝑢𝑒 𝑎̀ 𝑙𝑎 𝑡𝑒𝑐ℎ𝑛𝑜𝑙𝑜𝑔𝑖𝑒 𝑑𝑒 𝑞𝑢𝑏𝑖𝑡, 𝑏𝑎𝑠𝑒́𝑒 𝑎̀ 𝑇𝑒𝑙 𝐴𝑣𝑖𝑣).
Intel développe des qubits de spin en silicium depuis 2015 avec ses équipements de fabrication conventionnels.
Point de vue : L'acquisition de Classiq déplace l'enjeu du calcul quantique : la question n'est plus quelle technologie matérielle gagnera, mais qui contrôle la couche logicielle qui rend l'ensemble utilisable par un développeur ordinaire.

🔹 Procede Software (𝑒́𝑑𝑖𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟 𝑑𝑢 𝐷𝑀𝑆 𝐸𝑥𝑐𝑒𝑑𝑒® 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑐𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒𝑠 𝑑𝑒 𝑐𝑎𝑚𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑠, 𝑟𝑒𝑚𝑜𝑟𝑞𝑢𝑒𝑠, 𝑏𝑢𝑠 𝑒𝑡 𝑎𝑓𝑡𝑒𝑟𝑚𝑎𝑟𝑘𝑒𝑡) rachète RIMSS (𝑒́𝑑𝑖𝑡𝑒𝑢𝑟 𝑑𝑒 𝐷𝑀𝑆 𝑝𝑜𝑢𝑟 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑐𝑒𝑠𝑠𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑛𝑎𝑖𝑟𝑒𝑠 𝑎𝑔𝑟𝑖𝑐𝑜𝑙𝑒𝑠, 𝑑𝑒 𝑐𝑜𝑛𝑠𝑡𝑟𝑢𝑐𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛 𝑒𝑡 𝑑𝑒 𝑡𝑟𝑎𝑛𝑠𝑝𝑜𝑟𝑡, 𝑖𝑛𝑡𝑒́𝑔𝑟𝑎𝑡𝑖𝑜𝑛𝑠 𝑂𝐸𝑀 𝐾𝑢𝑏𝑜𝑡𝑎, 𝐶𝑎𝑠𝑒 𝐼𝐻, 𝐴𝐺𝐶𝑂 𝑒𝑡 𝐻𝑖𝑛𝑜).
Les deux plateformes sont construites sur technologie Microsoft. De nombreux groupes de concessionnaires opèrent à la fois des activités camion (Excede) et agricoles ou de construction (RIMSS).
Point de vue : La complémentarité est directe : réunir les deux DMS sous un même éditeur simplifie contrats, intégrations et support pour les groupes multi-activités qui utilisaient déjà les deux plateformes séparément.

Today’s fundraising briefing — 3 deals, the strategies behind them · 27 October 2026

🔹 Ailytics (real-time operational and security monitoring software from existing video streams, compatible with older cameras) — $7.4m · Series A.
Our view: The presence of Safie and a major Japanese manufacturer as investors signals that these are not financial investors betting on a trend, but players with construction sites and camera networks securing access to the technology.

🔹 Strawberry (web browser with integrated AI assistants to automate repetitive office workflows, CRM, meeting tracking, lead generation) — $6m · Seed.
Investors: General Catalyst and EQT Ventures (co-leads).
Our view: What General Catalyst and EQT Ventures are funding is less a proven product than a position in an emerging category: the browser as an orchestration layer for AI agents.

🔹 Karta AI (inbound conversational voice agents for large financial services companies, autonomous processing of complex requests) — $3m · Seed.
Founded by Vijaypal Singh and Abhishek Kushwaha, Karta AI already serves over 120 enterprise clients in banking, insurance, and financial services, including PhonePe, Pine Labs, InCred Finance, Bajaj Auto Credit, and Aavas Financiers.
Investors: PeerCapital and Cedar Hill Capital (co-leads); Wyser VC, CDM Capital, Seedstars.
Our view: The coverage of 25 languages is a real operational differentiator in the Indian market, where financial services customers speak Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Marathi, or Bengali, not a marketing argument.
